surveyDefinition.title: Video Streaming Subscriptions — consumer survey (Europe)
surveyDefinition.whatThisSurveyIs: A business-to-consumer (B2C) market research questionnaire about Video Streaming Subscriptions. Every question asks about Video Streaming Subscriptions specifically — not the wider market, not adjacent categories, and not any named brand. It is designed to tell a client what buyers in Europe actually do and want in this category.
surveyDefinition.whoseContextThisIs: Adults in Europe who buy or use Video Streaming Subscriptions for personal or household use. Respondents qualify if they: Currently has an active paid subscription to at least one video streaming service (e.g., Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Disney+, Hulu, HBO Max, etc.); Primary decision-maker or co-decision-maker for household streaming subscriptions; Aged 18 or older; Able to complete an online survey in the relevant language. Excluded: Individuals who only use free ad-supported streaming (e.g., free tier of Pluto TV, YouTube without subscription); Businesses or institutions purchasing streaming for commercial use (e.g., bars, hotels, offices); Cable/satellite TV subscribers who do not also have a streaming subscription; Children under 18 (unless surveyed via parent proxy, which is out of scope for this consumer survey).
surveyDefinition.whyTheseRespondents: Video streaming subscriptions are purchased by individual consumers and households for personal entertainment use. While some business plans exist, the dominant and defining market is consumer subscription services (e.g., Netflix, Disney+, Hulu).
respondentBehaviours: Streams video content at least weekly
Subscribes to one or more paid streaming services
Engages with original content and on-demand viewing
May churn or rotate subscriptions based on content library
whatIsDeliberatelyNotAsked: Age or household income — these define who was recruited, not what is measured, so they appear in the audience definition rather than as questions.
Brand, company or manufacturer names — the survey stays at category level so findings are not tied to one competitor set.
Where the respondent lives — region is chosen when viewing the results, so asking it again would waste a question.
surveyDefinition.howToReadTheNumbers: Percentages are simulated from a persona-weighted panel of 2,500 synthetic respondents built from real market evidence, not from fieldwork. Single-choice, ranking and rating-scale questions sum to 100%. Multi-select questions do not — each option is an independent share of respondents choosing it. The N shown on each question is the display base for that item.

structure.storyline: Questions run in a planned narrative order: broad and easy first, specific and sensitive last.
structure.storylineSummary: The survey opens by establishing the respondent's relationship with video streaming subscriptions and their viewing context, then moves into the practical details of how they discover, choose, and pay for subscriptions, including rotation and spend. It then explores their preferences and expectations for content, features, and value, before finally assessing satisfaction, friction, switching triggers, and future intent. The story progresses from broad, safe questions about usage to more sensitive topics like spend, trade-offs, and satisfaction, ending with forward-looking intentions.

targetCustomer.summary: Adult consumers of Video Streaming Subscriptions in Europe — who Currently has an active paid subscription to at least one video streaming service (e.g., Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Disney+, Hulu, HBO Max, etc.); Primary decision-maker or co-decision-maker for household streaming subscriptions; Aged 18 or older; Able to complete an online survey in the relevant language. The core consumer market for video streaming subscriptions is individuals and households who pay for access to on-demand video content. This audience is defined by active paid subscription and personal use, excluding free tiers and commercial buyers.

contextDemographics.income_band: Middle to upper income (household income $40k+ in developed markets)
contextDemographics.household: Individuals and households with internet access and connected devices (smart TV, smartphone, tablet, computer)
contextDemographics.geography: Global, with higher penetration in urban and suburban areas

assumptions: The segment refers to consumer-facing streaming services (e.g., Netflix, Hulu, Disney+) rather than B2B white-label or enterprise streaming platforms.
The survey targets the individual subscriber or household decision-maker, not all household members.
Geographic scope is global, but survey feasibility may require country-specific sampling.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes your current situation with paid video streaming subscriptions?
options: I have one paid video streaming subscription
I have more than one paid video streaming subscription
I do not have any paid video streaming subscription right now, but I have had one in the past 12 months
I have never had a paid video streaming subscription

data.label: I have one paid video streaming subscription
I have more than one paid video streaming subscription
I do not have any paid video streaming subscription right now, but I have had one in the past 12 months
I have never had a paid video streaming subscription

questions.insight: Top response: I have more than one paid video streaming subscription (52.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Family planners, mainstream entertainers, and premium enthusiasts drive multi-subscription; budget-conscious and value-seeking rotators contribute to churn/never groups.

questions.question: How central is video streaming to your overall TV and movie viewing?
options: It is my main way of watching TV and movies
It is one of several ways I watch TV and movies
It is a small part of how I watch TV and movies
I rarely or never watch TV and movies through streaming

data.label: It is my main way of watching TV and movies
It is one of several ways I watch TV and movies
It is a small part of how I watch TV and movies
I rarely or never watch TV and movies through streaming

questions.insight: Top response: It is my main way of watching TV and movies (55.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Cord-never urbanites, tech-savvy cord-cutters, and budget bingers rely heavily on streaming; older mainstream personas still use linear TV.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, which of the following situations have you watched streaming content in? Select all that apply.
options: Watching alone, fully focused on the screen
Watching with family or household members
Watching while doing other things (e.g., chores, working, scrolling)
Watching on a mobile device while out of the house

data.label: Watching alone, fully focused on the screen
Watching with family or household members
Watching while doing other things (e.g., chores, working, scrolling)
Watching on a mobile device while out of the house

questions.insight: Top response: Watching alone, fully focused on the screen (78.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Alone and background viewing are high across all personas; family co-viewing driven by family planners and mainstream entertainers; mobile viewing by young urbanites and tech-savvy.

questions.question: In a typical week, how many hours in total do you spend watching content on video streaming subscriptions?
questions.insight: Top response: 4 to 6 hours (30.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Budget bingers and cord-never urbanites skew higher hours; family planners moderate; older mainstream lower.

questions.question: Who in your household is mainly responsible for choosing which video streaming subscriptions to have?
options: I share this responsibility with someone else in my household
No one in particular / it just happened

data.label: I share this responsibility with someone else in my household
No one in particular / it just happened

questions.insight: Top response: I am (55.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Individualistic personas (young urbanites, tech-savvy) say 'I am'; family personas share or defer to partner.

questions.question: How much do you agree or disagree with the following statement: 'I often watch streaming content just to have something on in the background while I do other things.'
questions.insight: Top response: Agree (35.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Budget bingers and young urbanites often watch in background; cinephiles and premium enthusiasts disagree.

questions.question: Which of the following events or situations most recently prompted you to start or add a new video streaming subscription?
options: A specific new show, movie, or season I wanted to watch
A free trial or promotional offer
A recommendation from friends or family
A bundle with my phone, internet, or TV package
A live sports event or match I wanted to watch
I don't remember / None of the above

data.label: A specific new show, movie, or season I wanted to watch
A free trial or promotional offer
A recommendation from friends or family
A bundle with my phone, internet, or TV package
A live sports event or match I wanted to watch
I don't remember / None of the above

questions.insight: Top response: A specific new show, movie, or season I wanted to watch (42.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Content-driven personas (Family Planner, Mainstream Family, Cinephile, International Explorer) dominate; sports fans and bundle beneficiaries contribute smaller shares.

questions.question: In the last 12 months, which of the following have you done with your video streaming subscriptions? Select all that apply.
options: Re-subscribed to a service I had cancelled before
Rotated between services (cancelled one and started another)

data.label: Re-subscribed to a service I had cancelled before
Rotated between services (cancelled one and started another)

questions.insight: Top response: Started a new subscription (65.00%).
questions.distributionNote: High churn and rotation driven by Value-Seeking Rotator, Budget-Conscious Binger, and Cord-Never Young Urbanite; family personas less likely to cancel.

questions.question: Before you decided on your most recent video streaming subscription, where did you learn about or compare your options? Select all that apply.
options: Streaming service websites or apps themselves
Word of mouth at work or school
I didn't compare options—I just picked one

data.label: Streaming service websites or apps themselves
Word of mouth at work or school
I didn't compare options—I just picked one

questions.insight: Top response: Recommendations from friends or family (55.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Social proof and online research are common across most personas; tech-savvy and value seekers use comparison sites, while mainstream family relies on word of mouth.

questions.question: In the past 12 months, which of the following ways have you used to sign up for or pay for a video streaming subscription? Select all that apply.
options: Directly through the streaming service's own website or app
Through an app store (like Apple App Store or Google Play)
As part of a bundle with my internet or mobile phone provider
Through a third-party streaming aggregator or platform
With a prepaid gift card or subscription card from a retail store
Through a cable or satellite TV provider

data.label: Directly through the streaming service's own website or app
Through an app store (like Apple App Store or Google Play)
As part of a bundle with my internet or mobile phone provider
Through a third-party streaming aggregator or platform
With a prepaid gift card or subscription card from a retail store
Through a cable or satellite TV provider

questions.insight: Top response: Directly through the streaming service's own website or app (70.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Direct sign-up is dominant across all personas; app store and bundles are secondary, with Bundle Beneficiary and less tech-savvy users more likely to use bundles.

questions.question: In total, approximately how much do you spend per month on all video streaming subscriptions for your household? Please include the cost of any add-ons or premium tiers.
questions.insight: Top response: €10 to under €20 (30.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Middle-income personas cluster in €10-30 range; premium and tech-savvy users push upper end, budget-conscious keep low.

questions.question: When choosing which video streaming service to subscribe to, how important is each of the following factors?
options: Access to a wide variety of content

data.label: Access to a wide variety of content

questions.insight: Top response: Access to a wide variety of content (35.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Content variety and convenience are top drivers across all personas; exclusivity and ad-free are more important to premium and cinephile segments.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes how you typically decide whether to keep or cancel a video streaming subscription?
options: I review each subscription regularly and decide based on what I've watched recently
I only reconsider when I get a price increase or billing notice
I keep subscriptions on autopilot and rarely think about them
I cancel as soon as I finish the show I subscribed for
I rotate subscriptions based on what new content is coming out

data.label: I review each subscription regularly and decide based on what I've watched recently
I only reconsider when I get a price increase or billing notice
I keep subscriptions on autopilot and rarely think about them
I cancel as soon as I finish the show I subscribed for
I rotate subscriptions based on what new content is coming out

questions.insight: Top response: I review each subscription regularly and decide based on what I've watched recently (30.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Value seekers and budget bingers actively manage; mainstream family and premium enthusiasts are more passive; rotators drive the rotation option.

questions.question: Which of the following features would you consider a must-have for any video streaming subscription you pay for? Select all that apply.
options: Offline downloads to watch without internet
Multiple user profiles for different household members
Ability to watch on multiple devices at the same time
Parental controls to restrict what children can watch
None of the above — I don't consider any feature a must-have

data.label: Offline downloads to watch without internet
Multiple user profiles for different household members
Ability to watch on multiple devices at the same time
Parental controls to restrict what children can watch
None of the above — I don't consider any feature a must-have

questions.insight: Top response: Ability to watch on multiple devices at the same time (61.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Family planners and mainstream family entertainers drive parental controls and profiles; tech-savvy and premium users drive 4K and multi-device; budget-conscious and rotators are less demanding.

questions.question: How important is it that a video streaming service offers a large library of titles from different countries and languages?
questions.insight: Top response: Very important (36.00%).
questions.distributionNote: International content explorer and cord-never young urbanite strongly value international libraries; mainstream family and budget segments are moderate; premium cinephiles also push importance.

questions.question: When deciding whether a show or movie on a streaming service is worth your time, how much do you rely on each of the following signals?
questions.insight: Top response: Recommendations from friends or family (24.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Social recommendations dominate across family and budget segments; cinephiles and premium enthusiasts weight production quality and critics; trend-driven young urbanites boost popularity.

questions.question: Thinking about how you watch, which of the following best describes your preferred way to access a streaming subscription?
options: A single, all-in-one subscription that includes everything
A basic subscription that I can add extra channels or content packs to
A subscription that lets me rent or buy individual titles on demand
A free, ad-supported subscription that I don't pay for
A subscription that I share with friends or family to split the cost

A basic subscription that I can add extra channels or content packs to
A subscription that lets me rent or buy individual titles on demand

questions.insight: Top response: A single, all-in-one subscription that includes everything (38.00%).
questions.distributionNote: All-in-one appeals to mainstream families and premium users; add-on model fits tech-savvy and rotators; sharing is strong among budget-conscious and young urbanites; free tier attracts budget segment.

questions.question: How important is it to you that a video streaming service offers a substantial amount of content originally produced in Europe (including your own country)?
questions.insight: Top response: Very important (30.00%).
questions.distributionNote: International content explorer and quality cinephile drive high importance; mainstream family and eco-conscious also value local content; premium enthusiasts are less focused on origin.

options: I would not pay for a subscription under any circumstances

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied are you with your main video streaming subscription?
questions.insight: Top response: Somewhat satisfied (38.00%).

questions.question: Compared with what you expected when you first subscribed, how would you rate your main video streaming subscription?
questions.insight: Top response: About as expected (45.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Mainstream and family personas find service about as expected; premium and cinephile personas slightly better due to content quality.

questions.question: Which one of the following would be most likely to make you cancel or switch your main video streaming subscription?

metadata.storyline_summary: The survey opens by establishing the respondent's relationship with video streaming subscriptions and their viewing context, then moves into the practical details of how they discover, choose, and pay for subscriptions, including rotation and spend. It then explores their preferences and expectations for content, features, and value, before finally assessing satisfaction, friction, switching triggers, and future intent. The story progresses from broad, safe questions about usage to more sensitive topics like spend, trade-offs, and satisfaction, ending with forward-looking intentions.
storyline_notes: Adapted the canonical arc for a subscription service: replaced 'restock/replacement' with 'subscription cycle and rotation' to capture churn and rotation behavior, which is key in streaming.
Added a beat on 'subscription channels' to reflect the reality that streaming subscriptions are often obtained through bundles (telecom, device) in Europe, not just direct sign-ups.

In the preferences section, replaced generic 'format and packaging' with 'plan format and packaging preferences' to address ad-supported tiers, bundles, and family plans, which are central to streaming.
Added 'content credentials and origin' to reflect the European emphasis on local and original content, and the growing creator economy.
In the satisfaction section, kept the canonical order but ensured 'switching triggers' comes after 'friction' and before 'recommend intent' to maintain a logical flow from problems to actions.
All beats are answerable with closed questions and avoid asking age, income, geography, or brand names, per the rules.
